Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old patient with 2-day history of wheeze and shortness of breath after dust exposure while cleaning; symptoms worse at night and occasionally limit ability to complete sentences; history of childhood asthma and seasonal hay fever; advised urgent in-person evaluation for pulse oximetry and consideration of antihistamine and possible steroids.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing and shortness of breath.
- Onset/duration: Began ~2 days ago after cleaning with significant dust exposure; started about an hour after cleaning.
- Course/progression: Persistent over 2 days; worse at night; patient increasingly concerned today.
- Severity/impact: Sometimes unable to complete sentences when speaking due to breathlessness.
- Exacerbating/initiating factors: Likely dust exposure.
- Relieving factors: None reported; has not taken any medication for current episode.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies chest pain with deep breaths.
  - Denies dizziness/vertigo.
  - Eating and drinking adequate; estimates 4–5 glasses of water/day.
- Systems review/pertinent negatives: No pain on deep inspiration; no dizziness; no other systemic symptoms discussed.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (childhood), mostly resolved; occasional symptoms with prolonged running.
  - Associated medications: Has an asthma inhaler (type/dose/route/frequency not documented); not used for this episode. Prior history of taking steroids for asthma (details not documented).
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) in summer; typically does not take medications for it.
- Allergies: No known allergies reported.

Social History:
- Setting: Telehealth visit; environment private/quiet.
- Access to care: “Minutes’ drive” to a doctor’s surgery (exact travel time not documented).
- Tobacco, alcohol, recreational substances: Not discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: None documented (teleconsultation; video connection lost during call).

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Planned: Pulse oximetry at in-person visit (finger device to assess oxygen saturation). Additional testing as per GP/clinic assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute wheeze and shortness of breath likely triggered by dust exposure; differentials include allergic reaction vs asthma exacerbation.
  - Plan:
    - Attend GP/clinic in person for evaluation today; measure oxygen saturation with pulse oximetry and further assessment.
    - Consider antihistamine (over-the-counter) en route if available; if not, to be prescribed at clinic.
    - Possible need for steroids to be determined after in-person assessment.
    - Provider will send a letter via the app for the GP; anticipated clinic visit duration ~10 minutes.
- General plan items:
  - No emergency precautions or additional therapies documented.
  - No changes to current medications documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: 
  - Vital signs, peak flow/spirometry, lung auscultation.
  - Full medication list and doses (including inhaler type and dosing).
  - Detailed allergy clarification (drug vs environmental).
  - Smoking/alcohol/substance use history.
- Internal conflicts: None significant; patient owns an inhaler but confirmed not using any medication for this episode (not a conflict).
- Transcript quality: Occasional audio gaps/ellipses and a brief video loss; one incomplete time reference (“minutes’ drive”) and a truncated phrase (“check your …”).
